answer: Trust propagates through fixed-length random walks on the attestation graph, weighting identities by paths reachable from honest roots rather than raw counts. A sybil cluster with few links to the honest graph has low conductance—boundary weight relative to its volume—so bounded walks from those roots rarely enter it, limiting its aggregate sampled voting weight. Deduplication and decay prevent a velvet plume of copied claims from making relic attestations count as independent support.
